claim: [L29,L35,L46,L58] (HIGH/upload-failure-propagation) Transfer return codes are ignored and diagnostics discarded, allowing failed uploads to produce success messages and a download index containing unavailable binaries.
other_wording: [L52-L58] (MED/error-handling) Transfer output and exit status are discarded, allowing failed uploads to be reported as finished and an index to be published for missing artifacts.

claim: [L14,L21-L24] (MED/path-parsing) Discovery and path splitting assume bindir ends with a separator, so a normal directory argument without that suffix can shift platform and configuration fields or match sibling prefixes.
other_wording: [L14-L27] (MED/input-contract) Glob results are parsed using a raw prefix replacement and fixed path positions without validating the platform/configuration layout or supported configuration names.

claim: [L55-L58] (HIGH/shell-command-construction) Paths, username, and password are concatenated unquoted into a shell command, so spaces or metacharacters can change transfer arguments or execute unintended commands.
other_wording: [L55-L58] (MED/shell-quoting) Paths, credentials and destination are concatenated unquoted into a shell command, so spaces or shell metacharacters can alter command interpretation.

claim: [L14-L15,L19-L20,L40-L46] (MED/publication-completeness) An empty glob result still replaces the download page with an empty list and reports copying complete.
other_wording: [L14-L15,L37-L46] (LOW/empty-input) An empty artifact glob still publishes an empty download index without reporting that no binaries were found.

claim: [L14-L15,L20-L29] (MED/artifact-identity) Every zip in a configuration directory is uploaded under the same revision-derived name without checking its provenance, so stale or multiple archives can overwrite the intended release.
other_wording: [L20-L33] (MED/artifact-collision) Multiple ZIP files in one platform/configuration directory receive the same destination name and overwrite each other.

claim: [L57] (LOW/output-escaping) The source path is interpolated into a TeamCity message without escaping service-message delimiters or line breaks.

[L68,L81,L90-L96] (MED/publication-completeness) Missing configuration directories are silently skipped and the download index is still replaced, so incomplete or entirely absent build outputs can publish an incomplete or empty release page.
other_wording: [L68,L85-L96] (LOW/empty-input) Missing configuration directories are silently skipped and an empty index is still uploaded when none exist.

claim: [L40-L41] (HIGH/upload-failure-propagation) The upload subprocess return code is ignored and both output streams are discarded, allowing failed binary transfers to be reported as finished and listed in the published index.
other_wording: [L37-L41,L77-L83,L96] (MED/error-handling) Discarded transfer status and diagnostics allow failed uploads to appear successful and leave the published index pointing at absent artifacts.

claim: [L119-L125] (MED/archive-layout) Every archive entry uses only fname, flattening nested directories and creating duplicate names or breaking relative-path dependencies.
other_wording: [L121-L125] (MED/archive-layout) Every archived file uses only its basename, flattening subdirectories and permitting duplicate member names that lose the original directory structure.

claim: [L38-L41] (HIGH/shell-command-construction) Executable paths, credentials, and transfer paths are interpolated unquoted into a shell command, so spaces or shell metacharacters can corrupt arguments or execute unintended commands.
other_wording: [L40-L41] (MED/shell-quoting) Unquoted interpolation of executable paths, credentials and transfer paths into a shell command breaks on spaces or shell metacharacters.

claim: [L24-L26,L40] (MED/ignored-configuration) connect stores the requested port but put never passes it to pscp, so nondefault SSH ports are ignored.
other_wording: [L24-L28,L40] (MED/ignored-argument) The connection port is stored but never supplied to pscp, so a nondefault port is silently ignored.

claim: [L287-L305] (MED/graphics-api-assumption) Contour extraction assumes contourf exposes patch children with scalar FaceVertexCData, so graphics implementations with different contour objects can leave the polygon arrays empty and make reindexing fail.
other_wording: [L287-L298] (MED/graphics-portability) Contour reconstruction assumes contour objects expose patch children with scalar FaceVertexCData, making the helper dependent on a particular graphics-object representation.

claim: [L316-L322] (MED/polygon-topology) Removing all NaN separators before creating one patch joins separate polygon rings and can fill regions or holes that the original contour kept separate.
other_wording: [L316-L322] (MED/polygon-topology) Removing NaN separators before creating a patch joins disconnected polygon segments and can fill regions that should remain separate.

claim: [L300-L305] (MED/contour-identity) Polygons are matched only by contour level, so multiple disconnected polygons at the same level reuse one matching patch and can lose or duplicate geometry.
other_wording: [L300-L305] (MED/contour-mapping) Reordering patches by contour level alone collapses distinct same-level contours and uses unchecked zero indices when a level has no match.

claim: [L41-L46,L59-L64,L87-L92] (MED/graphics-handle-portability) Line handles are assigned into arrays initialized as numeric empty arrays, which is incompatible with MATLAB graphics versions that return object handles.

other_wording: [L21-L22] (MED/shell-quoting) Generated redirection and move commands do not quote filenames, so spaces or shell metacharacters in discovered filenames break the commands.

claim: [L21-L22] (HIGH/generated-script-data-loss) The generated batch file unconditionally moves the redirected .new file over the original even if findent fails or is unavailable, potentially replacing source with empty or partial output.
other_wording: [L21-L22] (MED/destructive-error-handling) The generated batch script overwrites each original source with the temporary output even when findent fails or produces incomplete output.

claim: [L5,L9,L13,L19] (LOW/working-directory-contract) Input discovery and output location depend on the caller's current directory rather than the MATLAB function's location, allowing invocation elsewhere to generate an empty or misplaced batch file.

claim: [L1002-L1004,L1073-L1075] (MED/empty-suite-reporting) The footer marks the previous test as crashed whenever no test ran, including a legitimate empty suite, and can duplicate the crash marker already emitted during restart.
other_wording: [L1002-L1004,L240-L242] (LOW/report-state) A run that executes no tests unconditionally appends a crash row, potentially duplicating a recovered-crash row or reporting a crash for an empty suite.

claim: [L399-L402,L474-L477,L527-L530,L607-L610,L660-L663,L1008-L1009,L1036-L1039] (MED/report-false-pass) Array size and shape mismatches increment nofails and invoke the hook but never update HTML failure state, so their test rows can be rendered as OK.

other_wording: [L174-L180] (MED/exit-status) Finalization executes a plain STOP regardless of failed assertions, leaving process-exit-based automation without a failure status.

claim: [L713-L715,L767-L768,L801-L802,L811-L812] (MED/comparison-truncation) Fixed-length line and token reads silently discard text beyond 200 characters per line or 20 characters per token, allowing differing files to compare equal.

other_wording: [L780-L795] (MED/failure-accounting) Premature EOF or a read error reports a failed comparison without incrementing nofails.

claim: [L155-L160,L220-L245,L109-L111,L137-L138] (HIGH/multi-suite-state) Every runtests call resets test numbering and reloads the previous suite's last_test, so the documented multiple-call workflow can skip tests in later suites and label completed work as crashed.

other_wording: [L443,L479,L532,L576,L612,L665] (MED/numerical-overflow) The sum of operand magnitudes can overflow before multiplication by the tolerance and falsely accept materially different large finite values.

claim: [L808-L824] (MED/parser-contract) List-directed tokenization errors are ignored and missing tokens use the real text sentinel '?', so malformed or slash-terminated records and literal question-mark tokens can hide differences.
other_wording: [L808-L824] (MED/parser-contract) Ignored list-directed tokenization errors and a literal question-mark sentinel can hide malformed or missing tokens, while numeric conversion uses only default-real precision.

claim: [L1050,L1124,L1175-L1178,L1493-L1498] (MED/output-escaping) Test descriptions, compared strings, and file contents are emitted as raw HTML, allowing ordinary angle brackets and ampersands to alter or conceal report content.
